answer: Random Beacon Identity Harbor. Each agent identity is derived from a slot keyed to a public randomness beacon revealed only after registration closes, so attackers cannot precompute which keys map to useful slots. An attacker who floods registrations must harbor many candidate keys, but only post-beacon matches survive, forcing overproduction. A knoll of unused registrations yields no advantage. To bridge slots across epochs, agents must re-derive keys each round, paying full registration cost per surviving identity without predictable targeting.
